results.content:
## What NotchNook did well

NotchNook was one of the first apps to turn the notch into something worth hovering. Its tray, AirDrop, calendar and webcam mirror set the pattern most notch apps follow, and a single one-time licence covered 5 Macs, which is generous.

## Where NotchDodo is different

NotchDodo leans towards getting work done. Alongside music, the shelf and your calendar, it puts a Pomodoro timer, tasks, notes, reminders, a calculator, screen time and live system stats in the notch, and every calendar event with a Zoom, Meet or Teams link gets a join button.

It is also the only notch app we know of that tracks Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI usage: tokens, estimated cost and your Claude Code 5-hour window, read from logs on your Mac.

# NotchNook alternative: NotchDodo vs NotchNook

NotchNook helped make the MacBook notch useful. As of late September 2026 it can't be downloaded, so here is an honest look at how NotchDodo compares if you're looking for something to use instead.

Facts checked 28 September 2026. We make NotchDodo, so read this knowing that.

### Pick NotchNookif

 You already have NotchNook installed and it still works for you.
 You want one licence for up to 5 Macs.
 You prefer its widget-style layout and deep customisation.
